event_name: Great Scottish witch hunt of 1661-1662 begins
significance: The great Scottish witch hunt of 1661-1662 began with the Restoration government's re-establishment of witch prosecution commissions, resulting in approximately 660 accused and roughly 300 executed in about eighteen months — the most intensive period of Scottish witch prosecution — and confirming Scotland's uniquely high per-capita rate of witch execution relative to English-speaking jurisdictions.
source_method: Scottish Privy Council records and presbytery archives; analyzed in Larner, Enemies of God (1981)
